Rashi on Arakhin 6b:10:1.hebrew: כל חרם לא יפדה - מי שהוא ראוי ליחרם וליהרג, אינו בכלל פדיון:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:10:1.english: “No devoted person shall be redeemed” - One who is liable to be condemned and executed is not included in [the category of] redemption.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:12:1.hebrew: למומתין בידי שמים - כגון האי דכתיב: "השור יסקל וגם בעליו יומת", והך מיתה ליכא למימר בידי אדם, דהא אמרי' בפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף טו:): "מות יומת המכה רוצח הוא" — על רציחתו אתה הורגו, ואי אתה הורגו על רציחת שורו:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:12:1.english: [With regard to] those executed at the hand of Heaven - Such as that which is written: "The ox shall be stoned, and its owner shall also be put to death," and this death cannot be said to be at the hands of man, as we say in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (15b): "The striker shall surely be put to death; he is a murderer" — for his [own] murder you execute him, but you do not execute him for the murder [committed by] his ox.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:13:1.hebrew: שלא ניתנה שגגתן לכפרה - כגון מגדף ומקלל אביו, דאם עשה בשוגג, אינו בקרבן ולא בגלות:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:13:1.english: Whose unwitting [transgression] was not designated for atonement - Such as a blasphemer and one who curses his father, for if he acted unwittingly, he is not [liable for] an offering nor [subject to] exile.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:13:2.hebrew: מיתות קלות - כלומר, דקלות להך מילתא שניתנה שגגתן לכפרה — כגון רוצח, דשגגתו גולה; ועובד ע"ז, ומחלל שבת, ובא על הערוה, דשגגתו חטאת:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:13:2.english: Lighter death penalties - That is to say, they are "lighter" in this regard: that their unwitting [transgression] was given over for atonement — such as a murderer, whose unwitting [act entails that he] goes into exile; and an idolater, a desecrator of Shabbat, and one who engages in forbidden relations, whose unwitting [act entails] a sin-offering.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:15:1.hebrew: כולי עלמא לא פליגי - דודאי נדרו נדר, והקדישו הקדש, ומעריך את אחרים, דהא בר דעה הוא:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:15:1.english: Everyone agrees - That certainly his vow is a [valid] vow, and his consecration is [a valid] consecration, and he [can] valuate others, for he is of sound mind.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:16:1.hebrew: מלוה על פה - כגון זה שהזיק, ולא עמד בדין על כך קודם למיתה. תשלומי נזק כתובין בתורה, ומדאורייתא משעבד ליה בעל כרחיה:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:16:1.english: An oral loan - Such as this [person], who caused damage and did not stand trial for it prior to [his] death. Payments for damage are written in the Torah, and by Torah law, [his property] is encumbered to [the injured party] against his will.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:18:1.english: And there are those who teach it - [This refers] to that [dispute] of Rav Yosef and Rabbah.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:18:2.english: [He is] liable - For he is a person of understanding.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:18:3.hebrew: פטורין - דאין לו דמים, ועומד הוא ליחבל. וכל הנך — איכא ליהרג בדיני ישראל קאמר:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:18:3.english: [They are] exempt - For he has no [monetary] value, and he is destined to be injured. And in all these [cases where one is] to be executed, it is speaking of [execution] under the laws of Israel.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:18:4.hebrew: לחזרת עמידת ב"ד - שאין אתה יכול להחזירו לב"ד ולעמוד בדין על מה שחבל, שאין מענין את דינו:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:18:4.english: To returning to stand [before the] court - For you cannot return him to court and [have him] stand trial for what he injured, as one does not delay his sentence.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:1:1.hebrew: רבי ינאי - גבאי הוה, ויזיף מעות הצדקה לצורכו ופרע:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:1:1.english: Rabbi Yannai - He was a charity collector, and would borrow charity money for his [own] needs and repay [it].

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:1:3.hebrew: דמעשה - רבי ינאי לציבורא, ואמר דלית ליה מעות לחלק לעניים, וכופה אותם לצדקה, ואיכא רווחא לעניים:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:1:3.english: That he compels - Rabbi Yannai [compels] the public, and says that he has no money to distribute to the poor, and coerces them [to give] charity, and there is a gain for the poor.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:2:1.english: A candelabrum - In its literal sense.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:2:2.english: A lamp - A croisel [an oil lamp] of silver or of gold.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:3:1.hebrew: מדאמר ר' אסי כו' - כלומר, מדנקט ר' אסי עובד כוכבים, דפעי וצועק: "למה שניתם ממה שנתתי?", מכלל דישראל, דלא פעי, שרי לשנויי לדבר מצוה; דאי בישראל אסור, ל"ל למנקט עובד כוכבים:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:3:1.english: From [the fact] that Rabbi Asi said, etc. - That is to say, since Rabbi Asi specified a gentile, who cries out and shouts, "Why did you change [the purpose of] what I gave?", by implication, in [the case of] a Jew, who does not cry out, it is permitted to change [it] for the purpose of a mitzvah; for if in [the case of] a Jew it were forbidden, why did he need to specify a gentile?

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:3:2.hebrew: שלא נשתקע שם בעליה - ממנה, שעדיין אומרים: "זו היא מנורה, נדבתו של פלוני עובד כוכבים":
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:3:2.english: [Before] its owner’s name has been forgotten - From it; that [people] still say: "This is the candelabrum, the donation of so-and-so, a gentile."

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:3:3.english: [It is] prohibited to change it - For he cries out [in protest].

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:4:1.hebrew: ולמאי - קאמר ר' אסי דאסור לשנותה? אילימא כו':
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:4:1.english: And for what [purpose] - Did Rabbi Asi say that it is forbidden to change it? "If we say," etc.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:7:1.hebrew: לא שכיח - שעזרק במתא דליפעי, שסוחר היה ומחזר בעיירות:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:7:1.english: [It is] not common - That Sha'azrak [would be] in the town to cry out [in protest], for he was a merchant and traveled about the towns.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:8:1.english: One who is moribund and one who is taken out to be executed, etc. - The Gemara explains the reason [for this].

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:8:2.hebrew: ר"ח בן עקביא - איוצא ליהרג פליג, אבל בגוסס מודה, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:ח׳): "והעמיד והעריך אותו", וגוסס לאו בר העמדה והערכה הוא:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:8:2.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Akavya - [It is] regarding one taken out to be executed [that] he disagrees, but regarding a moribund person he agrees, as it is written (Leviticus 27:8): "And he shall set [him] and valuate him," and a moribund person is not subject to setting [standing] and valuation.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:8:3.hebrew: שדמיו קצובין - בפרשה ערכין; אבל אנודר מודה, דהא כנמכר בשוק בעי למשיימיה, וזה אינו נמכר בשוק — כלומר, שאין אדם קונהו ויפסיד מעותיו:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:8:3.english: Because his value is fixed - In the [Torah] portion of valuations; but regarding one who vows [market value], he concedes, for behold, he must be appraised as [a slave] sold in the marketplace, and this [person] is not sold in the marketplace — that is to say, no person would buy him and lose his money.

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:8:4.hebrew: נודר ומעריך כו' - ובגמרא מפרש מאי קא אתי ר' יוסי למימר, הא ת"ק לא אמר "אינו נודר" — שאם אמר: "דמי פלוני עלי", יפטר — דהא "לא נידר" קאמר:
Rashi on Arakhin 6b:8:4.english: [He] vows and valuates, etc. - And in the Gemara [it] explains what Rabbi Yosei comes to say, for the first tanna did not say "[He] does not vow" — [meaning] that if he said, "The value of so-and-so is upon me," he would be exempt [from payment] — for he [only] said, "[He] is not the object of a vow."

Rashi on Arakhin 6b:9:1.english: Rather, [as for the ruling that] he is not valuated, why not? - Behold, his value is fixed [by the Torah].

Tosafot on Arakhin 6b:10:1.hebrew: מנין ליוצא ליהרג ואמר ערכי עלי שלא אמר כלום - ומשום דליתא בדמים ליכא למעוטי, דהא איתרבו לעיל (ערכין דף ב.) מנוול ומוכה שחין:
Tosafot on Arakhin 6b:10:1.english: "From where [is it derived regarding] one who is taken out to be executed and said, 'My valuation is upon me,' that he has said nothing" - And on account of [the fact] that he has no monetary value [damim], [one] cannot exclude [him], since above (Arakhin 2a) a disfigured person and one afflicted with boils were included [as subject to valuation].

Tosafot on Arakhin 6b:15:1.hebrew: כי פליגי באם הזיק - ובאם הקדיש לא פליגי, שמיד שהקדיש חל הקדש, ולא דמיא למלוה. אבל יש להקשות: אמאי לא פליגי באם נדר והעריך? וי"ל, דנקט הזיק משום דקתני חיוב בתשלומין (משום) [אהזיק], משמע דאהזיק לחודיה פליגי; ובנודר ומעריך — שמא יחול מיד, אבל גובה מן היורשין. ונודר ומעריך איצטריך, דס"ד: הואיל ואינו נידר ונערך, נודר ומעריך נמי אינו, קמ"ל דנודר ומעריך ומקדיש כשאר בני אדם:
Tosafot on Arakhin 6b:15:1.english: "When they disagree, [it is] in [a case] where he caused damage" - And in [a case] where he consecrated [property], they do not disagree, for immediately when he consecrated [it], the consecration took effect, and it is not similar to a loan. However, one can ask: Why do they not disagree in [a case] where he vowed or valuated? And one can say that [the Gemara] mentioned damage because [the Mishnah] teaches liability for payment [in connection with] damage, which implies that it is only regarding damage that they disagree; and regarding one who vows and valuates, perhaps [the obligation] takes effect immediately, but [in any event, an obligation to the Temple] is collected from the heirs [according to all]. And [stating that he] vows and valuates was necessary, for it might enter your mind to say: Since he cannot be the subject of a vow [nidar] or the subject of a valuation [ne'erakh], he also cannot vow [noder] or valuate [others]; [therefore, the Mishnah] teaches us that he vows, valuates, and consecrates like all other people.
